_note: DRAFT for wiring, robotic Moon landers. Same shape as the Apollo pilot json. Offsets are metres from the patch centre (= site point per the hotspot convention): lat_offset_m north+, lon_offset_m east+. px,py are in the 2048x2048 tier2-lroc.jpg (x right, y down, centre 1024,1024). Patch scale: m_per_px per site (see scale_basis). Hardware positions are by eye on the patch, checked against LROC captions/coordinates; no absolute coordinate was used to place a ring.

luna16.scale_basis: LROC Featured Sites page: pixel scale 0.55 m/pix; patch = centre 562x562 px of the 1000x562 featured_sites jpg, resized to 2048 (x3.644)

hotspot_annotations.label: Luna 16 descent stage
hotspot_annotations.confidence: one source (LROC Luna 16 featured image text + LROC Featured Site frame M141899500L whose feature pixel is the crop centre); object unmistakable: bright body with dark shadow in a blast halo
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The lower half of the Soviet Luna 16 lander, left on Mare Fecunditatis after the sample-return capsule lifted off on 21 September 1970 with about 101 grams of soil.

gallery.note: File:Luna 16 descent stage.png, NASA/GSFC/ASU, PD-NASA row; the LROC image with the descent stage inset

hotspot_annotations.label: Luna 17 lander
source: https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/402 (LROC "Lunokhod 1 Revisited": rover tracks around the lander, ramps on the east side)
https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/11 ("Enlargement of Luna 17 lander, note the Lunokhod 1 tracks starting at the ramp and circling the lander")
hotspot_annotations.confidence: two sources (LROC lander coordinate layer + LROC "Lunokhod 1 Revisited" text describing the lander with tracks circling it); LROC does not annotate this frame, identification by eye from the matching tracks-around-lander pattern
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The Luna 17 lander that delivered Lunokhod 1 to Mare Imbrium on 17 November 1970. Its descent engines brightened the surface around it, which makes the rover tracks circling the lander stand out.

change3.scale_basis: LROC Featured Sites page: pixel scale 1.559 m/pix, incidence 78.17 deg, slew -18.42 deg; centre 562x562 of the 1000x562 jpg to 2048

hotspot_annotations.label: Chang'e 3 lander
source: https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/637 (LROC: lander (44.1214 N, 340.4884 E) and rover from above, frame M1142582775R, image width 576 m)
https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/929 ("What a Blast!": lander, rover tracks and blast zone, frame M1147290066R)
hotspot_annotations.confidence: one source with a caveat (LROC 'Chang'e 3 Lander and Rover From Above', sibling frame M1142582775R taken the same pass 4 h earlier, lander = bright dot with dark streaks to its east); matched by that pattern. The dot is 50 m north of the patch centre although the patch centre is LROC's lander coordinate, so the registration or my match is off by that much. Medium confidence
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: China's Chang'e 3 lander, which touched down in Mare Imbrium on 14 December 2013, the first lunar landing since 1976. At this low Sun it shows as one bright pixel with a long shadow.

gallery.note: 'What a Blast! Revisiting the Chang'e 3 Landing Site' (LROC929), PD-NASA; lander with blast zone. Also missions/change3/05 (lander and rover arrows, LROC637)

dropped.reason: LROC places the rover about 44 m SE of the lander in sibling frame M1142582775R; in this frame the only candidate is a single bright pixel 50 m due south of the lander, which does not match that offset (about 20 m east missing). Frame is 1.56 m/px against a 1.5 m wide rover. Not annotated.
LROC (Clegg-Watkins 2016, post 929) shows them in frame M1147290066R; at incidence 78 deg in this frame nothing is resolved.

change5.baked_in_annotations: The patch carries LROC baked-in annotations (white box around the lander, label "Chang'e 5 lander", scale bar, frame id). A ring would sit inside the box.

hotspot_annotations.label: Chang'e 5 lander
hotspot_annotations.confidence: two sources (LROC 'First Look: Chang'e 5': 'The lander is the bright spot in the center of the outline' + the label drawn on this image; LROC-computed coordinates 43.0576 N, 308.0839 E +/-20 m)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: China's Chang'e 5 lander in Oceanus Procellarum, imaged by LRO the day after its 1 December 2020 touchdown. The sample-return mission brought back about 1.7 kg of lunar soil.

gallery.note: File:Chang'e 5 - After Blast Off (LROC1186), lander marked by an arrow, the ascender already gone; row credited CNSA/CC-BY-SA-4.0, image is an LROC product, credit to be checked

hotspot_annotations.label: Chang'e 6 lander
source: https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/1374 (LROC "First Look: Chang'e 6", frame M1472410644L, 7 June 2024)
hotspot_annotations.confidence: one source (LROC 'First Look: Chang'e 6': 'The lander is seen as the small cluster of bright pixels in the center of the image', on the rim of an eroded ~50 m crater; coordinates 41.6385 S, 206.0148 E +/-30 m)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: China's Chang'e 6 lander on the far side, in the Apollo basin, imaged by LRO about a week after its 1 June 2024 landing. The brighter ground around it was disturbed by the landing engine.

source: https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/1101 (LROC "Beresheet Crash Site Spotted!", frame M1310536929R, 22 April 2019)

hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The dark smudge where the Israeli Beresheet lander crashed on 11 April 2019 in Mare Serenitatis. It hit at a low angle, from the north, about 1000 m/s faster than planned; the smudge is about 10 m across and lowers the surface brightness by about 10%.
